title: Normalized finite free tower site comparison
statement: For a base P of [def-per-lisse-completed-system-data], continuous-coefficient IntegralReductionTower is equivalent to Systems, with a natural isomorphism between the actual underlying abelian diagrams and with compatibility with every constant integral scalar endomorphism. The structure NormalizedTowerSiteComparison records precisely these maps. This assertion contains no integral reconstruction and no rational realization.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1) and (4), with Corollary 5.1.5 for classical finite local systems; the comparison maps are reduction, inverse limit and localization. Their pullback and coefficient-extension compatibilities use these same maps. Etale-local existence of lattices is cited separately as an existing DAG node.

proof.text: Identify each continuous finite quotient coefficient ring with the constant quotient ring. Constant-ring module sheafification identifies its modules with fixed-ring module sheaves. For each $n$, apply [det-pe-finite-local-systems-twist] with the finite discrete ring $A_n$. It gives a fully faithful equivalence between etale and pro-etale local systems with finite module models. This restricts to finite locally free objects. Indeed, if a descended etale sheaf has constant model $P$ on a nonempty etale trivializing object, intersect its pullback with a finite-free pro-etale trivializing covering. On a nonempty member of this covering its constant model is both $P$ and $A_n^r$. Taking a geometric stalk and using [lem-weil-proetale-constant-sheaf-stalk] gives $P\cong A_n^r$. Empty covering members impose no condition. Conversely an etale finite-free trivialization remains one on the pro-etale site. Hence at each finite level the two locally free categories are equivalent, with quasi-inverse $\nu_{X,*}$ as specified in the cited equivalence.

source.place: Tag 099Y, label lemma-compare-locally-constant; compare Bhatt–Scholze Corollary 5.1.5, p.35

proof.text: This finite-level comparison also identifies normalized towers, not just their individual objects. Inverse image preserves colimits and tensor products by [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor]; tensor over a ring is the coequalizer imposing its balancing relations, so it preserves scalar extension along $A_{n+1}\to A_n$. Explicitly, the comparison sends the inverse image of $a\otimes x$ to the corresponding tensor of the inverse-image sections. Thus a normalization isomorphism pulls back to the normalization isomorphism. Conversely use [det-pe-finite-local-systems-twist] to descend every finite-level object. A transition map is descended uniquely by full faithfulness for the ring $A_{n+1}$: its target, originally an $A_n$-module, is regarded as an $A_{n+1}$-module and is still a finite local system. The descended normalization becomes an isomorphism after $\nu_X^*$, hence is an isomorphism since an equivalence reflects inverses. Uniqueness also descends all transition and morphism equations. Consequently finite-level comparison gives an equivalence of the two normalized tower categories. The inverse-image comparison on underlying abelian sheaves commutes with constant scalar endomorphisms. These canonical maps form diagramIso and its scalar equation.
